title: Internal resistance and terminal potential difference practice

question_set_contract.dependency_contract: Exactly two questions use Lesson 2: q01 direct retrieval and q07 mixed application.
question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: energy-per-charge retrieval, conceptual diagnostics, direct terminal-p.d. calculation, reverse internal-resistance calculation, then integrated current, voltage and power reasoning

evidence_basis.originality_note: All weather-station, inspection-lamp, gate-alarm and tracking-beacon contexts, wording, values and figure briefs are original.

questions.prompt: State what is meant by the e.m.f. of a source and by the potential difference across a component.
A real cell supplies current to one resistor. Which statement correctly describes its terminal potential difference V?

options.A: V is greater than the e.m.f. because charge gains energy in the internal resistance.
options.B: V equals the e.m.f. for every non-zero current.
options.C: V is less than the e.m.f. because energy per unit charge is transferred inside the cell.
options.D: V is less than the e.m.f. because charge is used up inside the cell.

questions.prompt: A source has e.m.f. 4.5 V and internal resistance 0.60 Ω. It supplies a current of 0.50 A. What is its terminal potential difference?

The external resistance connected to the same real source is increased, so the current decreases. The source e.m.f. and internal resistance stay constant. What happens to the terminal potential difference?

options.A: It decreases because the e.m.f. decreases.
options.B: It decreases because Ir becomes smaller.
options.C: It stays constant because current cannot affect voltage.
options.D: It increases because Ir becomes smaller.
